instruction: Review a tentative dual-brain duplex system for long multi-speaker conversations: interaction-controlled <pre_think> before a request, transition to <think>, partial-result sharing, and causal training-data construction including MultiTalkFT. A powerful text-only teacher generates private CoT from causally aligned transcripts to supervise an audio-conditioned thinking student p(z | x, c), with teacher p(z | x_text, c). Discuss overlooked details, using readable explanations and mathematical probability notation, in an HTML report sub-tab.
scope: Background preparation before an assistant-directed request, followed by interruptible request reasoning in a continuous multi-speaker conversation.
sub_questions: What can be prepared usefully before the actual request is known?
When should the interaction layer start, update, stop or resume background work?
What happens when a request or correction arrives during unfinished reasoning?
Which information should be private to S2 and which should reach S1?
How can existing dialogue data become causal scheduling and revision supervision?
How can causal transcript-conditioned teacher reasoning supervise the audio-conditioned student without future or speaker-information leakage?
How can evaluation separate background reasoning gains from memory, extra compute and easier input?

papers.problem: Reactive reasoning adds delay after each reply.
papers.method: Precompute likely next-turn reasoning; interrupt on arrival, then reuse or extend suitable work.
papers.results: Training-free evaluation in three time-aware dialogue environments.
papers.relevance: Closest precedent for the central idea.
papers.limitations: Predicting a next reply differs from maintaining a long, changing group conversation.

papers.method: Evaluate extraction, temporal reasoning, updates and abstention.

papers.method: Audio-conditioned student rollouts receive matched-text teacher guidance.
papers.relevance: Close precedent for the proposed conditional distributions and a later on-policy stage.
papers.limitations: Uses matched text and verified answers; our pre-request teacher must not see the future request or answer.

papers.problem: Reasoning must remain grounded in acoustic evidence.
papers.method: Modality-grounded reasoning distillation for audio tasks.
papers.results: Speech, sound and music reasoning evaluation.
papers.relevance: Motivates separate supervision for cues absent from transcripts.
papers.limitations: Clip-level reasoning is not our long multi-speaker preparation policy.
papers.title: Step-Audio-R1 Technical Report
papers.authors: Fei Tian, Xiangyu Tony Zhang, Yuxin Zhang, Haoyang Zhang, Yuxin Li, Daijiao Liu, Yayue Deng, Donghang Wu, Jun Chen, Liang Zhao, Chengyuan Yao, Hexin Liu, Eng Siong Chng, Xuerui Yang, Xiangyu Zhang, Daxin Jiang, Gang Yu

themes: Reasoning before the next input and interruptible asynchronous processing already have close precedents.
Structured state, conversation memory and request reasoning solve different problems and need separate controls.
An unfinished private reasoning trace is not automatically a grounded result or a resumable provider state.
Existing speech corpora supply conversations and timing, but not the proposed scheduling, validity and sharing labels.
Text-to-audio reasoning distillation has direct precedents; causal prefixes, partial-trace revision and group attribution remain the proposed extension.

gaps.statement: Whether selected background analysis improves later group-context answers beyond memory maintenance at matched compute.
gaps.evidence: These works cover anticipation, streaming state or memory individually; their inspected evaluations do not establish this combination.

gaps.statement: How to preempt, revise and reuse background notes under new multi-speaker evidence without stale speech.
gaps.evidence: Interruptible tools, S1/S2 handoff and group speech are established separately; the proposal needs a joint causal evaluation.

gaps.statement: Which small, grounded updates should reach S1 before a request, and whether training enables useful silence and clarification.
gaps.evidence: State sharing, late-result uptake, clarification, participation and privacy provide ingredients, rather than a verified unified policy.
